smell: ProxmoxCredentials.Zeroize is a security-critical lifecycle method (wipe password and APIToken bytes + nil out slices) with no test locking in (a) bytes are actually zeroed before nil, (b) nil receiver is safely handled, (c) idempotency on double-Zeroize. Breaking this silently leaks secrets in memory for the rest of the process lifetime.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — Zeroize IS the cred-lifecycle invariant (CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets: password fields as []byte with Zeroize lifecycle). Breaking it silently leaves cleartext in the heap slab across GC and could surface in a core dump.
fix_summary: Add internal/credentials/proxmox_test.go with: (1) TestZeroize_WipesPasswordAndToken — populate both, capture a byte-slice reference, call Zeroize, assert every byte is 0 via the captured alias (backed by the same underlying array), and assert c.Password/c.APIToken are now nil; (2) TestZeroize_NilReceiver — assert (*ProxmoxCredentials)(nil).Zeroize() does not panic; (3) TestZeroize_Idempotent — call twice, no panic. Stdlib testing only.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets: "Password fields in credentials.ProxmoxCredentials use []byte so callers can Zeroize them after use"
AUDIT_CONVENTIONS.md §13: "password fields as []byte with Zeroize lifecycle"
must_preserve: The nil-receiver guard at line 70-72.

smell: ProxmoxCredentials.String and GoString exist specifically to mask Password and APIToken from stray fmt.Sprintf/%v/%+v/%#v calls, but no test locks the invariant. A refactor that drops GoString (or flips Password from []byte back to string) would silently leak credentials via any log site that uses %+v.
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — a regression here directly produces cleartext-credential log lines. The masking is the single defensive barrier between %v in a stray slog call and a leaked token; untested == untrusted.
fix_summary: Add tests asserting (a) fmt.Sprintf("%v", creds) never contains the raw password or token bytes, (b) fmt.Sprintf("%+v", creds) also doesn't, (c) fmt.Sprintf("%#v", creds) also doesn't (GoString path), (d) nil receiver prints the nil literal. Table-driven with three inputs: password-only, token-only, both-set.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets: "Error messages must not leak raw credentials"
AUDIT_CONVENTIONS.md §13: credential scrubbing in error messages
must_preserve: The literal *** mask tokens (callers may grep for them).

smell: ProxmoxCredentials.Env produces the subprocess env-var snapshot that carries the raw password/token into Terraform. The branching (APIToken wins over Username/Password; Insecure conditionally appended; nil when !IsValid) is untested — a subtle bug (e.g. omitting PROXMOX_VE_ENDPOINT, or double-setting both auth styles) would mis-authenticate Terraform or leak the wrong credential path.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — Env is the bridge between cred []byte lifetime and the Terraform subprocess. Misformatted env → mis-auth; doubled env → ambiguous. The cred-handling path.
fix_summary: Table-driven TestEnv covering: (a) nil → nil, (b) token-only → [ENDPOINT, API_TOKEN], (c) user/pass → [ENDPOINT, USERNAME, PASSWORD], (d) both set → API token wins per UseAPIToken (lock the priority), (e) Insecure=true appends PROXMOX_VE_INSECURE=true, (f) Insecure=false does not emit the key. Verify by sorting and exact-match.
must_preserve: APIToken-wins priority in Env (matches GetProxmoxCredentials priority).

smell: GetProxmoxCredentials is the single chokepoint that decides where credentials come from (env vs config) and raises the EndpointFromConfig / ConfigCredentialsOverridden provenance flags — precisely the state the caller warns about. No test locks (a) env wins over config, (b) both-source warning flags fire, (c) APIToken / TokenID concatenation special-cases (the "tokenid=tokenid=secret" regression guard at line 204-206).
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — resolver for all downstream credential use. The "tokenid=tokenid=secret" guard is a regression-shaped comment explicitly present; untested means the next author deletes it.
fix_summary: Use t.Setenv to control env vars deterministically (Go 1.17+). Cover: (1) cfg nil → SourceNone, (2) env token set, config empty → SourceEnv, no flags, (3) env token set, config also has creds → SourceEnv + ConfigCredentialsOverridden=true, (4) env unset → SourceConfig, (5) APIToken with "=" + TokenID → no double concat, (6) APIToken without "=" + TokenID → prefix added, (7) missing PROXMOX_VE_ENDPOINT under env source → EndpointFromConfig=true, (8) host without scheme → https:// prepended + :8006 suffixed.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: roadmap.md references credential-provenance bugs this resolver guards against
must_preserve: Priority 1 (env) / Priority 2 (config) ordering; the tokenid= special case.

smell: WriteEnvFile persists the Proxmox password or API token to disk at mode 0o600 via AtomicWrite. There is no test locking (a) the file is created with 0o600 (attackers reading the .env would defeat the whole point), (b) absent fields are omitted, (c) password bytes from []byte land as the exact string. A future refactor that drops 0o600 or introduces an intermediate temp with wider perms would silently downgrade security.
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — writes cleartext credentials. A mode regression means world-readable secrets under an unexpected umask. This is exactly what LoadEnvFile's 0o077 perm-refusal check exists to defend against, but the write side has no test of its own.
fix_summary: Use t.TempDir + stat check: write creds, assert fi.Mode().Perm() == 0o600; also assert content line count matches present fields (APIToken-only path produces no PASSWORD= line; Insecure=false omits the line). Read-back and line-split assertion catches accidental CRLF or quoting changes.
rule_source: AUDIT_CONVENTIONS.md §13: "0o077-style tight perms on kubeconfigs, secrets, private keys"
repo-counter-example: envfile.go:106-111 (LoadEnvFile refuses 0o077 perms — the write side must match)
must_preserve: The 0o600 literal.

smell: loadEnvFileOnce refuses to load a .env whose perm bits allow group or other read (perm & 0o077 != 0). This check MUST run before godotenv.Load — any regression that swaps the order makes the check cosmetic. There is no test asserting (a) 0o644 is rejected with AuthError, (b) 0o600 loads, (c) missing file is silently ignored, (d) the rejection happens before the contents are read into memory.
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — the perm check is the load-bearing guard preventing okdctl from ingesting secrets the OS already published to other users. Breaking the check silently is a direct security regression.
fix_summary: Table-driven test with os.WriteFile + os.Chmod under t.TempDir: 0o600 → nil, 0o640 → AuthError(errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission)), 0o644 → same, 0o666 → same, missing path → nil. Because LoadEnvFile is guarded by sync.Once, use loadEnvFileOnce directly in tests (internal package access) to avoid fighting the Once across test cases.
must_preserve: 0o077 mask constant; the order (stat + perm check before godotenv.Load).

smell: AtomicWrite is the canonical trust-boundary file write (kubeconfigs, .env, hosts fragments) — temp-in-same-dir, Sync, Chmod to perm, Rename. No test locks (a) concurrent readers see old-or-new never partial, (b) the temp file is chmodded BEFORE rename (not after, which would leave a race), (c) on error the temp file is removed, (d) caller's perm is honored even when path pre-existed.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — AtomicWrite is explicitly listed in CLAUDE.md and AUDIT_CONVENTIONS §13 ("AtomicWrite + fsync on trust-boundary files"). It writes .env, kubeconfig, haproxy.cfg backups — breakage silently drops data or leaks perms.
fix_summary: internal/system/fs_test.go with: (1) TestAtomicWrite_WritesAndPerms — write, stat, assert content and Mode().Perm() == 0o600; (2) TestAtomicWrite_OverwritesWithNewPerm — pre-create path at 0o644, AtomicWrite with 0o600, assert the new perm is honored (regression guard for the explicit os.Chmod comment at line 197); (3) TestAtomicWrite_TempCleanupOnError — inject a writeFn failure (e.g. write to a read-only parent) and assert no .tmp-* files remain in dir; (4) TestAtomicWrite_MissingParent — creates it via EnsureDirForFile. Use t.TempDir throughout.
rule_source: AUDIT_CONVENTIONS.md §12 (canonical APIs) + §13 ("AtomicWrite + fsync on trust-boundary files")
must_preserve: fsync-before-rename ordering; chmod-before-rename (never after); temp-in-same-dir invariant.

smell: CopyFileMode is the canonical helper for copying credential-bearing files (kubeconfig, install-config.yaml, private keys) — creates dst with mode at open time and explicitly chmods if dst pre-existed. No test locks (a) mode is applied at creation under a permissive umask, (b) the post-Close chmod fires when dst pre-existed with different perms, (c) destination is removed on mid-copy failure, (d) Sync happens before Close.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — AUDIT_CONVENTIONS §13 explicitly lists "CopyFileMode over Create+Chmod" as a never-weaken invariant. Used for kubeconfig and install-config copies where a regression would briefly publish secrets at umask-default perms.
fix_summary: Add TestCopyFileMode covering: (1) fresh dst + umask 022 + mode 0o600 → final perm 0o600 (no window-wise race because of O_CREATE mode); (2) pre-existing dst at 0o644 + mode 0o600 → asserts post-Close chmod tightens it (the regression-guard comment); (3) source-missing → error and no dst created; (4) mid-copy disk full simulation via a read-only dst → dst is removed on failure. Use umask(022) in test setup via syscall.Umask.
must_preserve: The explicit os.Chmod at line 131 (the regression guard).

smell: WriteTempFile is the canonical temp-file-with-callback helper — chmod to mode, invoke writeFn, and on error close+remove. No test locks (a) writeFn failure removes the file, (b) chmod failure removes the file, (c) on success the caller owns cleanup (file still exists after return), (d) file is created with the requested mode (not default 0600 from CreateTemp).
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — CLAUDE.md names WriteTempFile as the canonical helper; it is called from ignition/pull-secret paths. A regression that leaves temp files on error would leak credentials across test runs and across reboots.
fix_summary: Add TestWriteTempFile: (1) success path — callback writes data, asserts file exists post-return, stat mode matches (e.g. 0o600), content matches; (2) callback-error path — inject errors.New in callback, assert returned error wraps cb error and filepath does not exist (os.Stat returns IsNotExist); (3) ensures the returned path is inside os.TempDir() so the caller's defer os.Remove targets the right file.
must_preserve: cleanup() calls on both error branches.

smell: ChownByName's comment explicitly states "numeric-only forms are rejected so config typos surface as errors rather than silently chowning to UID 0" — a security-critical invariant with no test. Accepting "0:0" silently would chown the destination to root, exactly the scenario the guard prevents.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — the "reject numeric → fail loud rather than chown to 0" is an explicit security invariant in the doc comment; unguarded by a test it will erode.
fix_summary: Test only the string-validation branch (not the actual chown to avoid root-required work): feed "0:0", "root:root" (integer lookup via user.Lookup which DOES resolve the string "root", so the rejection is purely numeric-form-based per the doc — lock the current behavior), "", ":", "foo:", ":bar". Assert error matches "invalid owner spec" for the malformed cases. For the valid-name case ("nobody:nogroup"), skip on CI if user lookup isn't available.
must_preserve: The exact error message prefix "invalid owner spec" (callers may switch on it).

smell: refuseCriticalPath is the defense-in-depth guard against a config typo pointing cleanup at /etc or /. It is called from SafeRemoveWithLogger, Dnsmasq, and the binary cleanup in packages.go. No test covers the allowlist — a regression (e.g. adding path with trailing slash, or switching from filepath.Clean to strings.HasPrefix) would silently let cleanup recurse into a system directory.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — the guard is the single thing standing between a typoed config and os.RemoveAll("/etc"). Untested means the next author could change filepath.Clean to strings.HasPrefix and bypass the whole protection. Analogous guard already HAS a test (refuseUnsafeISOPath), confirming the template.
fix_summary: Add internal/distribution/okd/cleanup/artifacts_test.go mirroring the refuseUnsafeISOPath test pattern: safe list ("/var/lib/okdctl", "/tmp/foo", "/home/user/work") expect nil, unsafe list ("/", "/etc", "/etc/", "/var", "/usr", "/lib/", "/bin", "/", "//etc", "/./etc") expect error. The trailing-slash and double-slash cases lock the filepath.Clean behavior that's load-bearing.
must_preserve: The criticalPaths slice and the filepath.Clean normalization.

smell: SafeRemoveWithLogger wraps os.RemoveAll with the refuseCriticalPath guard and a post-removal verification stat. No test covers (a) critical path is refused AND the returned error matches the guard, (b) non-existent path returns nil silently, (c) the post-removal stat-still-exists branch emits a warning and returns the "still exists" error — this is the destructive op's happy path and confirm-of-success.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — this is the only call point for os.RemoveAll in cleanup. The "removed but still exists" branch is an explicit invariant that detects chmod/bind-mount footguns; a regression that drops the post-stat silently reports success on a failed remove.
fix_summary: Augment the artifacts_test.go with: (1) TestSafeRemoveWithLogger_CriticalPath — path "/etc" → error matches "refusing to remove critical system path", actual /etc NOT touched (confirm via stat, though the guard prevents it regardless); (2) TestSafeRemoveWithLogger_MissingPath — nonexistent → nil; (3) TestSafeRemoveWithLogger_HappyPath — create file in t.TempDir, remove, assert not exists; (4) TestSafeRemoveWithLogger_DirWithContent — recursive remove via t.TempDir subdir with nested files. Use a testslog handler to capture warnings.
must_preserve: The post-removal stat check and its "still exists after removal" wording (downstream may grep logs).

smell: Execute is the entry point for okdctl destroy's file cleanup. The Kind dispatch (Full / WorkOnly / WebOnly / HAProxyOnly / TerraformOnly / unknown-default) decides WHICH directories get os.RemoveAll'd. No test covers (a) Full invokes every sub-phase, (b) WorkOnly only touches WorkDir, (c) unknown Kind returns the helpful error listing valid types, (d) individual sub-phase errors are joined not short-circuited.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — dispatch errors silently widen blast radius (a mis-routed Full deletes /var/www/html when the user asked for WorkOnly). The errors.Join behavior (continue-on-error) is load-bearing and undocumented-outside-code.
fix_summary: Use t.TempDir for WorkDir/HTTPServerRoot; test each Kind with observable side-effects (file created pre-test, assert removed or not removed). For unknown Kind, assert the error message lists all valid types (string.Contains). For the errors.Join invariant, inject a failure in one sub-phase (e.g. make WorkDir a read-only parent) and assert Execute returns non-nil but the other sub-phases still ran.
must_preserve: errors.Join continue-on-error behavior; the exact list of valid Kinds in the error message.

smell: Dnsmasq runs os.RemoveAll against paths produced by filepath.Glob("/etc/dnsmasq.d/okd-*.conf") and a secondary backup glob. Each match is guarded by refuseCriticalPath, but the glob + guard composition is untested — if an attacker plants /etc/dnsmasq.d/okd-../../etc file or similar (unlikely but shaped like a testable property), the current guard's filepath.Clean equality-check stance matters. No test locks the guarded-glob pairing.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — the glob targets /etc; a regression that drops refuseCriticalPath (it has been added retroactively per the nearby comments) would let a weird symlink turn this into a root-write primitive. Analogous guard tested elsewhere.
fix_summary: Because the hard-coded /etc/dnsmasq.d/... globs need root to exercise, refactor the glob/prefix pair into dnsmasqConfigGlobs() returning the two patterns, then test the guard-loop with a fake glob list: feed ["/etc/dnsmasq.d/okd-foo.conf", "/etc", "/"] into the guarded-remove helper and assert only the first reaches the (mocked) removeFn. The refactor isolates the guard logic at zero behavioral change.
must_preserve: Both glob patterns (config + backup); the refuseCriticalPath guard per iteration.

smell: processTarEntry is the zip-slip / symlink-escape guard around tar-archive extraction. It has THREE different escape checks (path-join stays-within-dest, directory EvalSymlinks, file-parent EvalSymlinks, symlink absolute-target refuse, symlink cleaned-target stays-within-dest). No test covers the attacker-shaped inputs: ../../../etc/passwd name; symlink with Linkname="../../../etc"; symlink followed by a regular file traversing through it; absolute symlink; directory whose EvalSymlinks resolves outside destDir.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path — CWE-22 / CWE-59. The comment at line 81-83 explicitly says the resolved-parent check exists to catch "writes that traverse a previously-extracted symlink". This is a textbook CVE class (GHSA patterns for zip/tar extraction); a test-less guard is a regression waiting to happen.
fix_summary: Construct an in-memory *.tar.gz via archive/tar + compress/gzip with crafted entries, then call ExtractTarGz into t.TempDir. Cases: (1) safe path; (2) ../../../etc/passwd entry → error contains "escape destination"; (3) absolute symlink target /etc → error "absolute symlink target not allowed"; (4) relative symlink target ../../.. → error "symlink target escapes destination"; (5) symlink to . followed by entry through the link → caught by verifyResolvedPath (the regression-guard comment); (6) directory entry that is actually a symlink to /tmp → EvalSymlinks catches. This is the #1 security test the repo is missing.
must_preserve: All three escape checks + the absolute-symlink refuse.

smell: FetchChecksum parses an HTTP-fetched checksums manifest for a filename match. The parser strips leading "*" and "./" and accepts suffix matches ("/filename"). No test locks (a) malformed hex rejected, (b) hex-length mismatch rejected, (c) suffix vs exact match (an attacker who controls the checksum server could exploit a substring-match mistake), (d) limit-reader cap at maxChecksumFileSize prevents memory blow-up, (e) comment lines are skipped.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path — checksum parser is a supply-chain trust boundary. An attacker who influences the checksums body (or a comment-line handling bug) could deliver a malicious binary whose computed sha matches a mis-parsed line. The hex validation already guards this; a test prevents regressions.
fix_summary: Because FetchChecksum takes a URL, refactor to a parseChecksumsBody(body []byte, filename string) (string, error) and test the parser directly with table-driven inputs: (a) exact match; (b) suffix match "subdir/file"; (c) leading "*"; (d) leading "./"; (e) comment-# line skipped; (f) hex short by 1 rejected; (g) non-hex chars rejected; (h) filename not found; (i) multiple matches returns first; (j) 2MiB body silently truncated at maxChecksumFileSize. The httputil-driven wrapper becomes two lines.
must_preserve: Hex validation (length + DecodeString) and the exact-match-before-suffix-match behavior.

smell: ValidateChecksum is the caller-facing integrity check for downloaded artifacts (ISOs, release tarballs). No test locks (a) empty expected → no-op nil return (this is a safety-critical default: a typoed config variable must not cause silent "no checksum, all good"), (b) mismatch returns an error containing both expected and actual (downstream logs depend on this format), (c) file-missing surfaces an error.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path — the empty-checksum → nil return is a deliberate escape hatch; if it ever changes (e.g. to fail-closed) every downloader caller that omitted a checksum breaks, but more importantly if it flips silently to "accept anything" callers think they're validated when they aren't.
fix_summary: TestValidateChecksum: (a) empty expected → nil; (b) matching checksum → nil; (c) mismatch → error message format contains both values; (d) missing path → error wraps os.Open failure. Use t.TempDir + write a deterministic small file, compute sha256, feed it.
must_preserve: Empty-expected → nil semantics and the error-message format.

smell: BuildOpaqueSecret is the canonical Opaque-Secret manifest builder called from flux and secretstore addons. No test locks the YAML shape: apiVersion v1, Kind Secret, type Opaque, namespace/name placement, data-value base64 encoding (the Secret type does it on marshal — if someone swaps sigs.k8s.io/yaml for gopkg.in/yaml.v3 the encoding breaks silently).
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — CLAUDE.md names this as the canonical k8s Opaque Secret builder; two addons call it today with actual credentials in the data map. Regression = broken addon secrets, possibly silent (kubectl apply would reject, but the builder ships a manifest that embeds the value wrong).
fix_summary: TestBuildOpaqueSecret: feed name+namespace+data={"username":[]byte("admin"),"password":[]byte("p@ss")}. Parse the returned YAML into a map[string]any and assert: apiVersion="v1", kind="Secret", type="Opaque", metadata.name/namespace, data.username == base64("admin"), data.password == base64("p@ss"). Covers the serialization invariant without faking the whole k8s type system.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: "addon.BuildOpaqueSecret is the canonical k8s Opaque Secret manifest builder"
must_preserve: type=Opaque; base64 encoding of data values via sigs.k8s.io/yaml.

smell: OcResourceExists is the canonical "does X exist?" helper for kubectl/oc checks across phase code. No test locks (a) empty stdout → false, (b) non-zero exit → false (with --ignore-not-found this is the usual path), (c) whitespace-only stdout → false (the TrimSpace), (d) transport error is wrapped with errPrefix. Callers depend on these semantics to decide whether to create-or-skip — a mis-implementation creates duplicate resources or skips required ones.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — CLAUDE.md names OcResourceExists as the canonical helper. Used throughout postinstall / install for idempotency; a regression causes duplicate creates or missed reconciles.
fix_summary: Requires a fake executor.Executor. Suggest: define a small interface in kubectl.go (type ocRunner interface { Run(ctx, name string, args ...string) (*executor.Result, error) }) and swap BasePhase.Exec via a constructor option — then tests inject a stub. Alternatively, extract the response-interpretation into a pure helper ocExistsFromResult(result, err, prefix) (bool, error) and test the pure helper exhaustively. The latter is the 3-line change.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: "BasePhase.OcResourceExists and BasePhase.OcPollOutput are the canonical kubectl/oc helpers"
must_preserve: --no-headers --ignore-not-found argv appends; the stdout TrimSpace check.

smell: OcPollOutput is the canonical "poll oc until predicate" helper. No test covers (a) predicate never matches → wait.WaitFor timeout error, (b) predicate matches on first call → captured value returned without polling, (c) non-zero exitcode skips predicate evaluation (so a transient kubectl error doesn't falsely satisfy), (d) ctx cancellation propagates.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — CLAUDE.md names OcPollOutput alongside OcResourceExists. Time-sensitive, intertwined with the exec package; the exitcode-check is a subtle invariant (an error on kubectl CANNOT look like a match).
fix_summary: Same refactor as OcResourceExists — a small ocRunner-style interface or a pure polling-predicate helper. Once that exists, use Go 1.25 testing/synctest (already flagged for WaitFor by audit-concurrency con:97cb8adf) to cover: (a) first-call match → no time advanced, (b) third-call match → two ticker intervals advanced, (c) timeout → DeadlineExceeded, (d) non-zero exitcode never matches. Shared synctest harness with the WaitFor tests.
must_preserve: The exitcode-before-predicate short-circuit.

smell: WaitFor is the poll primitive used by every OcPollOutput/WaitForBootstrap/cluster-ready check. Audit-concurrency (con:97cb8adf) already flagged it as a testing/synctest opportunity; audit-tests owns the "no test exists" finding per seam #9. Critical invariant at line 64-78: when ctx and timeout fire simultaneously, ctx.Err wins (comment explicitly states this).
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — WaitFor is called transitively from every "wait for cluster X" site; the ctx-wins-over-timeout invariant is load-bearing for error-taxonomy mapping (audit-errors err:ae5b624c depends on it). Synctest makes the test cheap and deterministic.
fix_summary: Use testing/synctest.Run (Go 1.25) to fully control time. Cases: (1) check() returns true on first call → no ticker advance needed; (2) check() returns true on Nth tick → advance N*Interval; (3) timeout with no cancel → opts.Timeout advances, error wraps nothing (format-only); (4) ctx cancel mid-poll → cancel at mid-interval, assert ctx.Err wrapped; (5) ctx-cancel-AND-timeout simultaneously → assert ctx wins (the load-bearing invariant). Shared helper for OcPollOutput test above.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: audit-concurrency con:97cb8adf already scoped this
must_preserve: ctx-wins-over-timeout at lines 64-67 and 75-78.

smell: MonitorInstallation is the canonical ctx-cancel-reap-goroutine pattern for openshift-install monitoring. Has a ticker-driven CSR approval loop, a kill-with-reap path, and three exit branches (installDone success, installDone error with ctx-wrapping, ctx-done kill-and-reap). Audit-concurrency (con:ae5b624c) already scoped the synctest opportunity; audit-api-design (api:fde34e0c:concrete-return-k8s) scoped the interface extraction that makes a test tractable; audit-tests owns the "no test exists" row.
evidence:
ticker := time.NewTicker(opts.CSRApprovalInterval)
// ...
case <-ctx.Done():
	killInstall()
	reapTimer := time.NewTimer(30 * time.Second)
	select {
	case <-installDone:
	case <-reapTimer.C:
		p.Log.Warn("install: process did not exit after kill, abandoning reap")
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — the reap-with-deadline pattern will recur (audit-concurrency suggested promoting it). The ctx.Err-preserving error wrapping at line 95-100 is exactly what audit-errors fixed upstream (err:ae5b624c). Test-less == at risk of regression that silently mis-maps exit codes.
fix_summary: Requires the csrApprover interface extraction from api:fde34e0c. Once MonitorInstallation accepts a csrApprover + an injected command runner, use testing/synctest to cover: (a) installDone(nil) → final ApprovePendingCSRs called, returns nil; (b) installDone(err) under ctx.DeadlineExceeded → error wraps DeadlineExceeded; (c) installDone(err) under ctx.Canceled → error wraps Canceled; (d) ctx cancel → kill + reap within 30s succeeds; (e) ctx cancel + kill ignored → 30s elapses + warn logged. Stub runner never actually launches a process.
must_preserve: sync.Once guard; buffered cap-1 installDone; 30s reap; ctx-wrapping pattern.

smell: ProxmoxBareHost strips port/scheme from a host string before feeding it to ssh. No test covers the adversarial inputs: host="https://px:8006", host="[::1]:8006" (IPv6 bracket form), host="user@px" (which ssh.SSHRun wraps with root@ unconditionally — should fail closed), host="px:22:bogus", empty, or hostnames containing shell metacharacters. A bug here reaches the SSH argv untouched.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path — the output is concatenated into "root@"+host and passed as an ssh argv. A bug reaching "evil.com;rm -rf" through here isn't exploitable (exec.Command + argv) but an incorrect return for IPv6 addresses is a user-facing bug. The trust-boundary shape matches the audit scope.
fix_summary: Table-driven test with: (a) "px" → "px"; (b) "px:8006" → "px"; (c) "https://px:8006" → "px"; (d) "http://px" → "px" (no port); (e) "[::1]:8006" → "::1"; (f) "" → ""; (g) "px:not-a-port" → returns the original string (SplitHostPort fails, falls through). Lock the current fallthrough behavior so a "surprising" refactor fails the test.
must_preserve: Fallthrough behavior on SplitHostPort failure.

smell: ParseNodeRole converts untrusted input (Terraform output, YAML config) into a NodeRole that is then used verbatim in HAProxy backend templates and ignition URLs (per the package-level comment). No test covers the case-sensitivity invariant ("Master" is rejected, matching openshift-install), the unknown-value path, or empty string. A regression that case-folds here silently accepts "BOOTSTRAP" and mis-routes ignition.
severity_reason: Straightforward parser with a clear invariant (case-sensitive match). A bug would be caught by integration testing but a unit test is cheap and locks the invariant.
fix_summary: TestParseNodeRole: valid={"bootstrap":RoleBootstrap, "master":RoleMaster, "worker":RoleWorker}; invalid=["Master", "MASTER", "", "etcd", "control-plane", " bootstrap "]. For invalid assert error message contains "unknown node role".
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever
must_preserve: Case-sensitive match.

smell: CIDRToNetmask converts an IPv4 CIDR to dotted netmask form for HAProxy/dnsmasq templates. No test covers (a) /0 → 0.0.0.0; (b) /32 → 255.255.255.255; (c) /24 → 255.255.255.0; (d) /7 → 254.0.0.0; (e) IPv6 CIDR rejected; (f) malformed input rejected. A bug produces an invalid netmask in haproxy.cfg and the service refuses to start.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — the value feeds a template that's rendered to /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg and /etc/dnsmasq.d/*.conf. An off-by-one in the bit math silently publishes wrong routes.
fix_summary: Table-driven test with the six cases above plus "::/0" → error, "256.0.0.0/24" → parse-error. Lock the /0 → 0.0.0.0 special case (the `if bits > 0` branch).
must_preserve: The /0 special case and IPv6 rejection.

smell: ValidateIPRangeInCIDR asserts a proposed VM-IP range fits inside a CIDR. Used during setup to prevent a static-IP allocation from spilling out of the machine network. No test covers (a) valid in-range, (b) start IP outside CIDR, (c) last IP (start + count-1) outside CIDR (boundary off-by-one), (d) count <= 0, (e) IPv6 rejected via start.Is4(), (f) malformed inputs.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — this validator is the ONLY thing standing between a typo'd config and a Terraform run that allocates IPs outside the bastion's network. Boundary bugs (start fits, start+count-1 doesn't) are classic off-by-one.
fix_summary: Table-driven: startIP=192.168.1.10, count=10, CIDR=192.168.1.0/24 → OK; startIP=192.168.1.250, count=10, CIDR=.0/24 → error listing end 192.168.2.3; count=0 → error; count=-1 → error; startIP=2001:db8::1 → error (Is4 false); startIP=10.0.0.1, CIDR=192.168.1.0/24 → "not within CIDR". Lock the boundary case.
must_preserve: The end = start + (count-1) semantics (inclusive range).

smell: CalculateVMIP adds index to startIP with an explicit uint64 overflow guard. No test exercises the overflow boundary (255.255.255.255 + 1 → error, 255.255.255.0 + 255 → .255 not overflow, 0.0.0.0 + 0 → .0). A regression dropping the uint64 guard silently wraps around and produces a valid-looking but wrong IP.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — the guard is explicitly noted as the reason the gosec G115 suppression is safe. Regressing the guard invalidates the suppression and produces wrap-around IPs in VM allocation.
must_preserve: The uint64 overflow guard (justification for the G115 suppression).

smell: ResolveVIP decides the cluster VIP: explicit value (after ParseAddr+Is4 validation) or derived from StaticIP.Start via the .10 last-octet convention. No test locks (a) explicit IPv6 rejected, (b) explicit IPv4 passes through canonicalized (netip.Addr.String() normalises things like leading zeros), (c) empty explicit falls back to derivation, (d) invalid staticIPStart surfaces the error.
severity_reason: The VIP flows into haproxy.cfg and dnsmasq config; a regression would produce an invalid listener. But this is a thin wrapper and the error path is easy to catch at first deploy — demote from major.
fix_summary: Table-driven: (explicit="192.168.1.10", staticStart="") → "192.168.1.10"; (explicit="2001:db8::1", ...) → error; (explicit="not-an-ip", ...) → error; (explicit="", staticStart="192.168.1.100") → "192.168.1.10" (derivation); (explicit="", staticStart="bad") → error.
must_preserve: The Is4 rejection of IPv6.

smell: isValidNetmask validates dotted or prefix-form netmasks, including the load-bearing contiguous-bits check (rejects 255.0.255.0). No test covers (a) /24 form, (b) 255.255.255.0 OK, (c) 0.0.0.0 rejected per the explicit comment, (d) 255.0.255.0 rejected (the non-contiguous case that motivated the bit-math), (e) 255.255.255.255 accepted (the inverted==0 branch), (f) IPv6 rejected.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — the bit-math expression is load-bearing and non-obvious. The comment shows the author worked through three forms; future edits without a test will drop the all-ones-accept branch or the 0.0.0.0-reject branch.
must_preserve: The 0.0.0.0 reject; the 255.255.255.255 accept; contiguous-bits check.

smell: ValidateProxmoxHost validates host-or-hostport strings from wizard/config input. Feeds ProxmoxBareHost which feeds ssh argv. No test covers (a) "px:8006" OK, (b) IPv6 "[::1]:8006" OK, (c) bare hostname "px" OK, (d) "px:abc" (non-numeric port) rejected, (e) "" rejected, (f) "https://px" rejected (scheme leaks — it's neither a valid hostname nor IP), (g) hostnames with shell metacharacters rejected (via isValidDomain regex).
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path — the validator is the trust boundary for Proxmox endpoint input; feeds ssh downstream. Regression that accepts "px;rm -rf" would be caught at ssh-argv level but a missed scheme or bracket-form bug surfaces as a confusing deploy failure.
fix_summary: Table-driven per AUDIT_CONVENTIONS §13 attacker-shaped inputs: ["px.example.com", "192.168.1.1", "192.168.1.1:8006", "[::1]:8006", "px:abc", "https://px", "px px", "../../etc", "", "px; id ;"] with expected pass/fail. Especially lock the "https://px" rejection (it contains ":" so SplitHostPort is tried, succeeds with h="https", "//px" which fails isValidHostOrIP — lock this chain).
must_preserve: The SplitHostPort-then-isValidHostOrIP chain.

smell: validateHAMasters enforces the etcd-quorum invariant (master count must be odd when > 1). No test covers the boundary: 1 OK, 2 reject, 3 OK, 4 reject, 5 OK, 0 OK (because the caller already rejects < 1 elsewhere — lock this delegation). A deploy with 2 masters will succeed setup but cluster will fail at etcd bootstrap with no actionable error.
severity_reason: Guards an operational invariant; mis-behavior produces a messy but recoverable failure at deploy time rather than data loss. Minor per rubric.
fix_summary: Six-row table: {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5} with {OK, OK, err, OK, err, OK}. Twelve lines of test.
must_preserve: The count>1 short-circuit (0/1 both pass).

smell: destroySteps orchestrates Terraform destroy + ISO removal + file cleanup + firewall cleanup. The ordering and NonFatal flags are the "safe to partial-fail" contract. No test covers (a) SkipTerraform=true skips the first step, (b) KeepISOs=true skips ISO removal, (c) a non-fatal step failure does not abort the rest, (d) the infra-destroy failure warns about --force file cleanup skip.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — destroy is by definition irreversible; an orchestration bug (e.g. firewall cleanup running before terraform destroy while VMs still exist) could lock operators out. The SkipWhen/NonFatal contract is load-bearing.
fix_summary: Refactor destroySteps to accept a testable dependency surface (terraform-destroyer interface, iso-remover interface, cleanup-runner interface, firewall-remover interface) via struct injection. Then test: (1) SkipTerraform=true, KeepISOs=true → only StepCleanupFiles, StepCleanupFirewall, StepPrintSummary enabled; (2) KeepISOs=false, Proxmox=nil → StepRemoveRemoteISO skipped with correct reason; (3) NonFatal step returns error → orchestrator proceeds to next step. Each row asserts the executed step IDs in order.
must_preserve: Step ordering; the NonFatal on ISO/cleanup/firewall but NOT on terraform (the ONE fatal step).

smell: InvokingUser/InvokingUserHomeDir resolve the original user under sudo re-exec. No test covers (a) SUDO_USER=valid → returns that user; (b) SUDO_USER=nonexistent (fallback to current user — doc says we don't fail); (c) SUDO_USER unset → current user. The fallback to current user on lookup failure is a deliberate design decision and is load-bearing: without it, a sudo re-exec where the user was deleted mid-run would fail the deploy.
severity_reason: The fallback-to-current-user behavior is documented in the comment but not tested; a regression that returns the error instead of falling back aborts late-stage deploy chown-back. Minor because the doc is clear and the fix surfaces at test time.
fix_summary: Use t.Setenv("SUDO_USER", ...). Cases: (a) unset → user.Current matches; (b) "root" (known valid) → returns root; (c) "definitely-not-a-real-user-xyz123" → falls back to user.Current without error. Skip the deleted-user-mid-run case as untestable without process-level sudo.
must_preserve: Fallback-to-current-user on lookup failure.

smell: invokingUserIDs parses SUDO_UID / SUDO_GID into ints. No test covers (a) both set → struct returned, (b) both unset → (nil, nil) — the load-bearing "no chown needed" signal, (c) SUDO_UID set but SUDO_GID empty → (nil, nil), (d) invalid numeric → wrapped error. The (nil, nil) case drives every ChownToInvokingUser call's no-op branch.
severity_reason: The (nil, nil) return is the way ChownToInvokingUser decides to no-op. A bug that returns a zeroed struct instead silently chowns to UID 0 — that's actually a blocker-ish path, but would be caught by ChownByName's numeric-reject sibling if used correctly. Keeping minor because the failure mode is mitigated elsewhere.
fix_summary: t.Setenv rows: both unset → (nil, nil); SUDO_UID=1000, SUDO_GID=1000 → {uid:1000, gid:1000}; SUDO_UID="abc" → error matches "invalid SUDO_UID"; SUDO_UID=1000, SUDO_GID="" → (nil, nil) (the either-empty → nil path).
must_preserve: (nil, nil) semantics when EITHER env var is empty.

smell: WriteAsInvokingUser combines AtomicWrite + chown-back. The "parent dir chowned iff it did not pre-exist" logic (line 84-86 + 94-96) is a subtle invariant — exists to avoid silently chowning a pre-existing dir the user created with different ownership. No test locks this.
severity_reason: Minor: the invariant is easily rediscovered from the comment. Still worth locking because a refactor that always chowns the parent is a plausible "simplification".
fix_summary: Skip the actual chown (root required); test only the parentExisted flag path by extracting the existence probe into a seam OR by checking behaviour via fs inspection. Minimal value unless the chown-back is mocked — consider this an acknowledgement rather than an emit-to-fix.
must_preserve: The parentExisted flag check (avoid silent re-chown).

smell: NewInsecure returns an HTTP client with InsecureSkipVerify=true, narrowly scoped to bootstrap-phase probes per the doc comment. No test locks that New() does NOT return an insecure client (i.e. the TLS config is nil or has InsecureSkipVerify=false). A refactor that factories out a shared transport could silently flip the invariant.
severity_reason: The invariant "New() is secure" is intuitive but worth locking. A regression would defeat TLS verification on every HTTP call the repo makes — but the caller landscape is small and the gosec suppression is present, so the blast radius is bounded.
fix_summary: TestNewVsNewInsecure: c := New(1*time.Second); assert c.Transport is nil (Go uses DefaultTransport which validates); d := NewInsecure(1*time.Second); assert d.Transport.(*http.Transport).TLSClientConfig.InsecureSkipVerify is true. Three assertions, no live network.
must_preserve: New() has no custom Transport; NewInsecure() HAS InsecureSkipVerify=true.

smell: ConfigureHAProxy writes to /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg — a root-required file on the live system — and has a rollback path that restores from backup on validation/restart failure. No test covers the rollback: (a) no prior config → no backup taken, no rollback; (b) validation fails → backup restored, service restarted with old config; (c) rollback chmod/restart failure surfaces joined errors. Silent rollback bugs leave the node serving broken haproxy.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — rollback is the only thing preventing a bad config from taking down the ingress. Untested means the next refactor that swaps CopyFile for os.Rename (non-cross-device-safe) silently breaks rollback, but only surfaces during a failed deploy when rollback is already exercised.
fix_summary: Requires swapping the hard-coded /etc/haproxy paths + ManageService subprocess calls for injected seams. Practical test: extract the rollback lambda into a package-local helper attemptHAProxyRollback(cause, haproxyCfgPath, backupPath, chmodFn, restartFn) error and table-drive: (a) restore fails → joined error; (b) restore OK, restart fails → joined; (c) happy rollback → cause returned. This is the high-risk, high-value rewire — flag for prioritization.
must_preserve: Rollback order: restore file → chmod → restart service. Joined-error semantics.

smell: destroyInfrastructure is the actual terraform destroy driver. No test covers (a) missing terraform env dir → clean error; (b) no state file → warn and return nil (no-op on previously-destroyed infra — this is the load-bearing idempotency); (c) destroy succeeds → cleanup called; (d) destroy fails → error wrapped with "terraform destroy failed" prefix (CLI layer depends on this string for exit code mapping).
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — destroyInfrastructure is THE hook that calls terraform destroy on live VMs. Idempotency (no-state → warn-not-fail) is load-bearing; a regression that errors on no-state breaks the "re-run destroy after partial failure" workflow.
fix_summary: Requires injecting the terraform facade (today it's constructed inline via terraform.New(...)). Refactor Phase to hold a terraformFactory func(dir) terraformOp where terraformOp has HasState/Init/Destroy/Cleanup. Then test: (a) dir missing → error; (b) HasState=false → nil + warn log captured; (c) Destroy returns err → wrapped error; (d) Destroy OK, Cleanup err → warn log only, Destroy success still surfaces. The injection is ~15 LOC of plumbing.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: UsePlan=true is a safer-pattern comment that must not silently revert
must_preserve: HasState=false → nil+warn; UsePlan=true; error-prefix string.

smell: ApprovePendingCSRs drives MonitorInstallation's CSR-approval loop. No test covers (a) PendingCSRs returns [] → (0, nil) fast path, (b) non-empty list → single `oc adm certificate approve` with all names in one argv (the batching is load-bearing — N separate approve calls per tick would rate-limit the API), (c) PendingCSRs error → (0, err) propagates; (d) runCheck failure wraps with "failed to approve CSRs" prefix.
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-wide-usage — ApprovePendingCSRs is called on every tick of MonitorInstallation's install-watch loop; it IS the bridge between node boot and a healthy cluster. Broken batching (one call per name) would break on clusters with >100 CSRs queued at bootstrap.
fix_summary: Swap c.run in k8s.go to accept a test injectable runner (it's already a method receiver — one field option would suffice). Table-driven: (a) 0 CSRs → (0, nil), 0 runs; (b) 3 CSRs → 1 run with argv ["adm","certificate","approve","csr-1","csr-2","csr-3"]; (c) PendingCSRs returns error → propagate; (d) runCheck returns error → wrapped. Seams nicely with api:fde34e0c:concrete-return-k8s (the csrApprover interface audit-api-design suggested).
must_preserve: Single-argv batching (all names in one approve call).

smell: redactConfig is the single credential-scrub barrier between `okdctl config show` / `okdctl debug-bundle` output and the user's terminal or support tarball. A regression that drops the TokenID masking (e.g. a refactor removing the explicit `px.TokenID = "***"`) silently emits the raw API token in every debug bundle. No test locks the mask.
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — this function is cited by CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets intent ("Error messages must not leak raw credentials") and is reachable from `debug-bundle` that users attach to support tickets. A regression produces a cleartext-token exfiltration path with no moving parts between the bug and the user.
fix_summary: Add internal/cli/config_test.go with: (1) TestRedactConfig_MasksTokenID — marshal redactConfig(cfg).Provider.Proxmox to YAML; assert output contains `token_id: '***'` and NOT the original token; (2) TestRedactConfig_NilProxmox — nil Provider.Proxmox is preserved; (3) TestRedactConfig_EmptyTokenID — empty string stays empty (not overwritten with ***); (4) TestRedactConfig_ReturnsCopy — mutating the result does not mutate the input. Stdlib testing + sigs.k8s.io/yaml (already imported).
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §credentials-and-secrets: "Error messages must not leak raw credentials"
must_preserve: The literal *** mask token and the exact json:"-" tags on Username/Password/APIToken in config.ProxmoxConfig — callers grep the output for ***.

smell: cleanupTerraformEnv deletes Terraform planfiles, .terraform.lock.hcl, and terraform.tfstate.backup but intentionally preserves terraform.tfstate (which is required to run `okdctl destroy` against existing infra). A refactor that accidentally adds `terraform.tfstate` to filesToRemove strands the cluster — the Proxmox VMs remain but Terraform no longer knows they exist, so `destroy` can't clean them up and the user has to `pvesh destroy` by hand. No test locks the exclusion.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — losing terraform.tfstate is the exact scenario CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes + the in-code comment warn against. The comment IS the invariant; untested, the next refactor is one copy-paste away from stranding every deployed cluster.
fix_summary: Add internal/distribution/okd/cleanup/infra_test.go: (1) TestCleanupTerraformEnv_PreservesTfstate — create a tmp dir containing `terraform.tfstate`, `terraform.tfstate.backup`, `tfplan`, `.terraform.lock.hcl`; call cleanupTerraformEnv; assert terraform.tfstate STILL exists and the other files are gone; (2) TestCleanupTerraformEnv_MissingDirNoError — non-existent envDir returns nil; (3) TestTerraform_EmptyEnvCleanAll — terraformEnv="" walks every child. Stdlib testing + testing/fstest OR direct os ops in t.TempDir.
must_preserve: The `// terraform.tfstate - KEEP THIS!` comment and the exclusion from filesToRemove.

smell: RemoveHAProxy calls os.RemoveAll(phase.DefaultHAProxyConfigPath) (= /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg) then tears down firewall rules, the bastion VIP, and verifies API reachability. The /etc removal has no guard against an attacker-influenced DefaultHAProxyConfigPath (currently a const, but consumed indirectly), no partial-failure test (what if firewall.RemoveRules fails?), no idempotency test (second call on an already-removed haproxy). One regression flips DefaultHAProxyConfigPath → crashes /etc.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss adjacent — a misconfigured DefaultHAProxyConfigPath could remove an arbitrary /etc subtree. Not blocker because the path is a compile-time const today, but the destructive semantics are untested and a future override (e.g. reading from config) would widen the blast radius silently.
fix_summary: Add postinstall/haproxy_test.go with a fake Exec / Log and an injectable haproxyConfigPath variable (apply the same test-injection pattern setup/haproxy.go uses). Cases: (a) happy path — service stopped, config file gone, firewall rules removed; (b) empty VIP skips the kube-vip verification branch; (c) os.RemoveAll error is logged but does not abort (resilience); (d) API-via-VIP wait returning non-ok yields *errtypes.NetworkError. Must use t.TempDir so no real /etc writes happen under `go test`.
rule_source: AUDIT_CONVENTIONS.md §13: tight perms / allowlist-style critical path checks
must_preserve: The warn-on-error resilience: all failures log and continue, except the VIP reachability wait which must error. Preserve httputil.NewInsecure here — kube-vip self-signs.

smell: cleanup.HAProxy deletes the live haproxy config, globs *.backup.* siblings, removes okdctl firewall rules, releases the bastion VIP, and uninstalls the haproxy package. The wildcard glob `haproxyConfig + ".backup.*"` is not tested for attacker-shaped haproxyConfig (e.g. `../../etc/shadow`) — a caller passing an unvalidated path propagates path traversal into os.RemoveAll via the glob expansion.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — SafeRemoveWithLogger is guarded by refuseCriticalPath, but the caller contract for HAProxy is not locked by a test. If a future refactor swaps SafeRemoveWithLogger for a raw os.RemoveAll, the glob becomes an arbitrary-file-delete primitive driven by caller input. Untested == unlocked.
fix_summary: Add cleanup/services_test.go::TestHAProxy_GlobOnlyMatchesBackups — populate t.TempDir with `haproxy.cfg`, `haproxy.cfg.backup.1`, `haproxy.cfg.backup.2`, `haproxy.cfg.orig` (not a .backup.*); pass tmpDir/haproxy.cfg as haproxyConfig with a nop logger and stubbed firewall/netutil/packages; assert only haproxy.cfg + .backup.* are removed, .orig survives. Include a TestHAProxy_RefusesCriticalPath with haproxyConfig="/etc/passwd" asserting the guard blocks removal.
must_preserve: The refuseCriticalPath guard via SafeRemoveWithLogger.

smell: ChownTreeToInvokingUser explicitly uses os.Lchown (not os.Chown) so a symlink inside the walk is chowned itself rather than its target. This is a security invariant (quoted in the function doc: "a malicious symlink cannot redirect the chown to /etc"). No test locks Lchown semantics — a regression swapping os.Lchown for os.Chown silently enables the symlink-redirect attack the contract defends against.
severity_reason: rubric §4/TOCTOU-adjacent — the Lchown-vs-Chown choice is the entire mitigation. Without a test, the invariant sits in a code comment that reviewers may mis-read. Attack requires local filesystem write into the workdir mid-run (narrow), so major not blocker.
fix_summary: Add internal/system/elevation_test.go::TestChownTreeToInvokingUser_LchownSemantics — build SUDO_UID/SUDO_GID to the current user (so chown is a no-op), create t.TempDir with a symlink pointing outside the tree (e.g. to /etc/hosts), call ChownTreeToInvokingUser. Assert: (a) the symlink target's mtime/ino is unchanged (stat the target pre/post), (b) the walk didn't error out on the symlink. Also a TestChownTreeToInvokingUser_NoSudoEnv returning nil without side effects.
must_preserve: os.Lchown and the //nolint:gosec suppression comment (both are load-bearing for the invariant).

smell: GenerateInstallConfig reads the pull-secret and writes install-config.yaml (containing the raw pull-secret JSON) at mode 0o600 via AtomicWriteString, then duplicates it to install-config.yaml.backup via CopyFileMode at 0o600. Both perm values are critical — the pull-secret is a Red Hat registry credential. A regression flipping either mode to 0o644 silently world-reads the credential until the file is consumed and removed. No test locks the perms on either file.
severity_reason: rubric §4/credential-exposure — install-config.yaml contains a live pull-secret (`.pullSecret` JSON blob). The 0o600 mode IS the only defense; broken canonical helper OR a caller arg flip silently world-reads it. Major (not blocker) because the file is short-lived (openshift-install consumes then manifests replace it), but the window is non-zero.
fix_summary: Add setup/ignition_test.go::TestGenerateInstallConfig_Perms — build a minimal cfg with cfg.Files.PullSecret + cfg.Files.SSHPublicKey pointing at tmp files; call GenerateInstallConfig with outputDir=t.TempDir; stat both install-config.yaml and install-config.yaml.backup; assert os.FileMode.Perm() == 0o600 for each. Also TestGenerateInstallConfig_PullSecretReadFail asserts *errtypes.AuthError on missing pull-secret.
rule_source: AUDIT_CONVENTIONS.md §13: tight perms on kubeconfigs, secrets, private keys
must_preserve: The 0o600 mode on both outputPath and backupPath; the errtypes.AuthError wrapping on pull-secret read failure.

smell: mergeKubeconfig + mergeNamedList implement the invariant that merging `okdctl kubeconfig --merge` into the user's existing ~/.kube/config must NOT overwrite an existing cluster/user/context with the same name (see mergeNamedList's `if !existing[name]` guard). A regression that flips the guard silently clobbers the user's production-cluster credentials with okdctl-generated ones. The file is written at 0o600 via AtomicWrite, but name-collision semantics are wholly untested.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — kubeconfig entries are credentials; clobbering a same-named cluster/user silently migrates the kubectl default to a different cluster's token. A user's `kubectl get pods` after merge would hit the wrong cluster with no visible warning. User-harm path.
fix_summary: Add internal/cli/kubeconfig_test.go with: (1) TestMergeNamedList_PreservesExisting — dest has cluster `prod`, src has cluster `prod` + `dev`; assert result contains dest's `prod` AND src's `dev`, not src's `prod`; (2) TestMergeKubeconfig_PreservesCurrentContext — dest has current-context=`prod`, src has `okd-test`; assert final current-context is still `prod`; (3) TestMergeKubeconfig_WritesAt0600 — stat the dest file after merge. Use a tmp KUBECONFIG env var via t.Setenv.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever (invariant in code == invariant in test)
must_preserve: The `!existing[name]` guard in mergeNamedList and the `existing == ""` guard on current-context. AtomicWrite at 0o600 for dest.

smell: ValidateTerraformEnv (regex `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`) is the ONLY barrier between user config input and filepath.Join(projectRoot, "infrastructure", "terraform", "environments", cfg.Deployment.TerraformEnv). A regression relaxing the regex (e.g. adding `.`) enables `../production-prod` traversal out of the environments dir. Attacker-shaped inputs (`../`, `./`, absolute paths, null bytes, unicode lookalikes, empty-after-trim) are untested.
severity_reason: rubric §4/known-exploit-path — config.Deployment.TerraformEnv flows directly into filepath.Join for terraform workdir discovery, plan/destroy, and cleanup. A traversal would cause destroy/cleanup to operate in the wrong directory (wrong state file → wrong cluster destroyed). Major (not blocker) because the wizard rarely accepts hand-crafted config and the regex holds today.
fix_summary: Add internal/config/validators_test.go::TestValidateTerraformEnv_AttackerShaped — valid: `production`, `staging`, `dev_cluster1`, `a`, empty (accepted as default); invalid (all must error): `../production`, `./prod`, `/absolute`, `prod/sub`, `prod with space`, `prod;rm -rf /`, `$(id)`, `\`id\``, `production\x00hidden`, "-starts-with-hyphen", "1starts-with-digit", ".dotfile". Table-driven.
must_preserve: The regex pattern `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` and the empty-string=>nil carve-out (callers rely on it for runtime default).

smell: terraform.Executor.Cleanup removes tfplan, destroy.tfplan, and terraform.tfstate.backup but NOT terraform.tfstate. The set of files-to-keep vs files-to-remove is an invariant identical to cleanupTerraformEnv, but declared in a different file — drift between the two lists is the exact class of bug that loses state. No test exercises the list.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — Cleanup() runs on the workdir that contains terraform.tfstate. The implicit invariant ("don't remove tfstate") matches infra.go's explicit comment, but neither is locked. A refactor adding `terraform.tfstate` to the list silently loses cluster state.
fix_summary: Add internal/infrastructure/terraform/terraform_test.go::TestExecutor_Cleanup_PreservesTfstate — create an Executor with WorkDir=t.TempDir containing tfplan, destroy.tfplan, terraform.tfstate, terraform.tfstate.backup.
